prompt:
Let \(X\) be a smooth, geometrically irreducible variety defined over \(\mathbb Q\).  
Suppose there exists a finite étale morphism  

\[
\pi : Y \longrightarrow X
\]

of degree \(d=12\) whose geometric monodromy group (the Galois group of the Galois closure of the function field extension) is the dihedral group  

\[
G = D_{12}= \langle r,s\mid r^{6}=s^{2}=1,\;srs=r^{-1}\rangle .
\]

The action of \(G\) on the geometric fibre \(\pi^{-1}(\bar x)\) (a set of 12 points) has **exactly two** orbits, each of size \(6\).

For a prime \(p\) of good reduction, let \(X(\mathbb F_p)\) and \(Y(\mathbb F_p)\) denote the sets of \(\mathbb F_p\)-rational points.  Define  

\[
L \;=\; \lim_{p\to\infty}\;
        \frac{1}{\# X(\mathbb F_p)}\,
        \sum_{x\in X(\mathbb F_p)} \#\pi^{-1}(x)\; .
\]

Compute \(L\).  Give the answer as a decimal number rounded to four decimal places.

Let \(G=\operatorname{PSL}(2,7)\), a group of order \(168\).  
Via its natural action on the projective line \(\mathbf P^{1}(\mathbf F_{7})\) it acts faithfully and transitively on the set \(\Omega\) of \(7\) points.

For a random element \(g\in G\) (chosen uniformly), let \(f(g)\) be the number of points of \(\Omega\) fixed by \(g\).
Define the limiting probability  

\[
P=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#\Omega(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in\Omega(\mathbf F_{p})}\mathbf 1_{\{\,\text{Frobenius at }p\text{ fixes }x\,\}},
\]

which, by the Chebotarev/Burnside principle, equals the proportion of elements of \(G\) that fix at least one point of \(\Omega\).

Compute \(100\,P\) and give the answer rounded to four decimal places.

Consider the projective space \(\mathbf{P}^{14}\) whose points correspond to homogeneous degree‑4 polynomials in three variables, i.e. to plane quartic curves in \(\mathbf{P}^{2}\).  
Let \(\Delta\subset\mathbf{P}^{14}\) be the discriminant locus, consisting of all singular quartic curves.

The degree of \(\Delta\) can be computed as the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle on the Grassmannian of lines in \(\mathbf{P}^{2}\); the result is the integer \(d\).

Determine this degree \(d\).  
Give your answer as a decimal number with exactly four digits after the decimal point (for example, write “27.0000”).

Let \( \mathbb P^{5} \) be the projective space whose points correspond to plane conics
\(C\subset\mathbf P^{2}\) (coefficients of a homogeneous quadratic form, up to scaling).
Fix five smooth conics \(C_{1},\dots ,C_{5}\) in \(\mathbf P^{2}\).
For a variable conic \(C\) denote by \(\Delta_{i}(C)\) the discriminant of the pair
\((C,C_{i})\); it is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2 in the coordinates of
\(\mathbb P^{5}\) and vanishes exactly when \(C\) is tangent to \(C_{i}\).

Assume the five conics \(C_{1},\dots ,C_{5}\) are generic, so that the five
quadrics
\[
Q_{i}=\{\,\Delta_{i}=0\,\}\subset\mathbb P^{5}\qquad(i=1,\dots ,5)
\]
intersect transversely.

**Question.**  
How many points does the intersection \(Q_{1}\cap Q_{2}\cap Q_{3}\cap Q_{4}\cap Q_{5}\) contain?
Give the answer as a decimal number rounded to four decimal places.

Let  

\[
f(x)=x^{4}-2\in\mathbb{Q}[x].
\]

For a prime \(p\neq 2\) let  

\[
N(p)=\#\{\,a\in\mathbb{F}_{p}\mid f(a)\equiv 0\pmod p\,\}.
\]

Define  

\[
L=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{1}{\pi(X)}\sum_{\substack{p\le X\\ p\ \text{prime}\\ p\neq2}} N(p),
\]

where \(\pi(X)\) is the number of primes \(\le X\).  
Compute \(L\) and give your answer rounded to **four decimal places**.  

(Assume standard conjectures guaranteeing the existence of the limit; you may use that the Galois group of \(f\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\) is the dihedral group \(D_{4}\) of order 8.)

Let \(X=\mathbb A^{1}_{\mathbb F_{p}}\setminus\{0,1\}\).  
For each \(t\in X(\mathbb F_{p})\) consider the sextic polynomial

\[
f_{t}(x)=x^{6}-t\,x^{3}+1\in\mathbb F_{p}[x].
\]

Let \(Y\) be the scheme over \(X\) whose fibre over \(t\) is the set of unordered
pairs \(\{\,\alpha,\beta\,\}\) of distinct roots of \(f_{t}(x)\) in \(\overline{\mathbb F}_{p}\).
For a generic value of \(t\) the Galois group of \(f_{t}\) over \(\mathbb F_{p}(t)\) is the
dihedral group \(D_{6}\) (order 12), acting in the natural way on the six roots;
consequently \(D_{6}\) acts on the 15 unordered pairs of roots.

Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#X(\mathbb F_{p})}
      \sum_{t\in X(\mathbb F_{p})}\#Y_{t}(\mathbb F_{p}),
\]

the average number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-rational unordered pairs of roots of
\(f_{t}\).  

Compute \(L\) and give the answer rounded to four decimal places.

Let  

\[
\mathbb P^{5}=\mathbf P\bigl(H^{0}(\mathbf P^{2},\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{2}}(2))\bigr)
\]

be the projective space whose points correspond to (possibly singular) plane conics.
Fix a smooth conic \(C_{0}\subset\mathbf P^{2}\).

Define  

\[
T_{C_{0}}=\{\,C\in\mathbb P^{5}\mid C\text{ is tangent to }C_{0}\,\}.
\]

The set \(T_{C_{0}}\) is a closed subvariety of \(\mathbb P^{5}\).
Determine the **degree** of \(T_{C_{0}}\) (the number of intersection points with a
general linear subspace of complementary dimension).  
Give your answer as a decimal number rounded to four decimal places.

Let  

\[
f(x)=x^{5}+x+1\in\mathbb{Z}[x].
\]

For each prime \(p\) at which \(f\) remains separable modulo \(p\) (i.e. \(p\neq 5\) and \(f\) has no repeated root in \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)), let  

\[
N(p)=\#\{\,a\in\mathbb{F}_{p}\mid f(a)\equiv 0 \pmod p\,\}
\]

be the number of roots of \(f\) in the field \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\).

Define  

\[
L=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{1}{\pi(X)}\sum_{\substack{p\le X\\ p\text{ prime}}} N(p),
\]

where \(\pi(X)\) is the number of primes \(\le X\) (the sum is taken only over those primes for which \(f\) is separable modulo \(p\)).

Compute \(\displaystyle \bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).  Give the answer as a decimal number with four digits after the decimal point.
